u0502.gist: India became the world's leading ship-recycling nation in 2025 with 35.4% of global ship recycling, meeting a Maritime India Vision 2030 target five years early.
facts: India's share of global ship recycling: 35.4% in 2025 (30.1% in 2024).
Data from UNCTAD, cited by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways on 22 June 2026.
Volume recycled: 2.99 million GT in 2025, up from 1.86 million GT in 2024.
Annual growth in recycling volume: nearly 60%.
Achieved a Maritime India Vision 2030 target five years ahead of schedule.
u0502.trap: 35.4% is the 2025 share; 30.1% is the 2024 share.

mcq.q: According to UNCTAD data cited by the Ports Ministry in June 2026, what was India's share of global ship recycling in 2025?
mcq.why: India accounted for 35.4% of global ship recycling in 2025, up from 30.1% in 2024.

u0503.gist: The Navy commissioned stealth frigate INS Mahendragiri, the sixth Project 17A ship, into the Eastern Fleet at Visakhapatnam on July 11, 2026.
facts: Commissioned July 11, 2026 at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, into the Eastern Fleet.
Sixth Project 17A stealth frigate commissioned within about 18 months.
Named after the Mahendragiri range, Eastern Ghats; motto 'Mighty, Majestic, Matchless'.
Built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL), Mumbai; designed by the Navy's Warship Design Bureau.
Over 75 percent indigenous; about 6,670 tonnes; speed up to 28 knots.
Project 17A (Nilgiri class): seven frigates, four by MDL and three by GRSE; seventh is Vindhyagiri.
u0503.hook: Mahendragiri motto = three M's: Mighty, Majestic, Matchless.
u0503.trap: Sixth Project 17A frigate commissioned overall, but the fourth built by MDL.

mcq.q: INS Mahendragiri, commissioned at Visakhapatnam in July 2026, is a frigate of which project?
mcq.why: INS Mahendragiri is the sixth Project 17A stealth frigate commissioned.

mcq.q: Which Project 17A frigate was still under construction when INS Mahendragiri was commissioned in July 2026?
mcq.why: The seventh ship, Vindhyagiri, was still under construction.

u0504.gist: On July 3, 2026, Sarbananda Sonowal unveiled the first India-made EXIM shipping container, built for Maersk, at the Maersk–CONCOR depot in Dadri, Uttar Pradesh.
facts: Unveiled July 3, 2026 by Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal.
Made for global shipping company A.P. Moller–Maersk.
Place: Maersk–CONCOR Inland Container Depot, Dadri, Uttar Pradesh.
Backed by the ₹10,000-crore Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme (Union Budget 2026–27).
Plan: raise yearly container-making capacity nearly tenfold to around 7.5 lakh TEUs.
Also: ICGS Achal ('firm'), an Adamya-class Fast Patrol Vessel, commissioned May 09, 2026 at Goa Shipyard.
u0504.hook: Dadri (UP) = first 'Made in India' export box, for Maersk.
u0504.trap: ICGS Achal = 'firm' (Adamya class, May 2026); ICGS Akshay = 'Indestructible' (June 2026).

mcq.q: Where was India's first indigenously manufactured EXIM shipping container unveiled in July 2026?
mcq.why: It was unveiled at the Maersk–CONCOR Inland Container Depot in Dadri, Uttar Pradesh.

mcq.q: India's first commercially procured India-made export container (July 2026) was built for which shipping company?
mcq.why: The container was manufactured for global shipping company A.P. Moller–Maersk.

u0505.gist: DRDO and the IAF conducted the maiden flight-trial of TARA, India's first indigenous glide weapon system, off the Odisha coast on 7 May 2026.
facts: TARA = Tactical Advanced Range Augmentation.
Maiden flight-trial by DRDO and the Indian Air Force off the coast of Odisha on 7 May 2026.
A modular range extension kit that turns unguided warheads into precision-guided weapons.
Designed by Research Centre Imarat (RCI), Hyderabad, with other DRDO labs.
Aim: raise the combat value of low-cost aerial weapons.

mcq.q: TARA, flight-tested in May 2026 as India's first indigenous glide weapon system, stands for:
mcq.why: TARA stands for Tactical Advanced Range Augmentation, a modular range extension kit.

u0506.gist: On May 24, 2026, Russia used its hypersonic Oreshnik ballistic missile during a mass drone and missile attack on Kyiv.
facts: Used by Russia on May 24, 2026 during a mass drone and missile attack on Kyiv.
Oreshnik means 'Hazel Tree': its warheads fall in streaks of fiery light.
Ukrainians called the first one fired 'Kedr' (Cedar).
Likely an intermediate-range ballistic missile; range 3,000 to 5,000 km.
u0506.trap: Oreshnik = Hazel Tree (Russian name); Kedr = Cedar (Ukrainian nickname).

mcq.q: What does the name of Russia's 'Oreshnik' missile, used against Kyiv in May 2026, mean?
mcq.why: Oreshnik means 'Hazel Tree'; Ukrainians called the first one 'Kedr' (Cedar).

u0507.gist: Cochin Shipyard delivered 'Malwan', a Mahe-class Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft, to the Indian Navy on March 31, 2026.
facts: Delivered March 31, 2026 by Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), Kochi.
Part of the Mahe-class ASW Shallow Water Craft project.
Named after Malwan, a historic coastal town in Sindhudurg district, Maharashtra.
Name reflects the maritime legacy of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
ASW SWCs detect and counter submarines in littoral (near-shore) waters.
u0507.trap: Delivery (31 March 2026) is not the same as commissioning.
u0507.check: The ship is spelt 'Malwan' here but 'Malvan' in the INS Malvan article (u0498).

mcq.q: The ASW Shallow Water Craft 'Malwan', delivered to the Indian Navy in March 2026, is named after a coastal town in which district?
mcq.why: CSL specified that Malwan is located in Sindhudurg district, Maharashtra.

u0508.gist: GRSE, Kolkata delivered Agray, the fourth of eight ASW Shallow Water Craft it is building, to the Indian Navy on March 30, 2026.
facts: Delivered March 30, 2026 at Kolkata.
Fourth of eight ASW SWCs being built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE), Kolkata.
About 77 metres long; class called the largest Indian Naval warships propelled by waterjets.
GRSE also delivered Sanshodhak, the fourth and final Survey Vessel (Large), for hydrographic surveys.
u0508.trap: Agray is built by GRSE (Kolkata), not by Cochin Shipyard like the Mahe-class ships.

mcq.q: Agray, an ASW Shallow Water Craft delivered to the Indian Navy on March 30, 2026, was built by:
mcq.why: Agray was indigenously designed and built by GRSE, Kolkata.

mcq.q: Sanshodhak, delivered by GRSE in 2026, is the fourth and final vessel of which class?
mcq.why: Sanshodhak is the fourth and final Survey Vessel (Large) of its class.

u0509.gist: India successfully test-fired the Agni-III intermediate-range ballistic missile from the Integrated Test Range, Chandipur, Odisha, on February 6, 2026.
facts: Test-fired February 6, 2026 from the Integrated Test Range, Chandipur, Odisha.
Agni-III: indigenous, two-stage, solid-fuelled IRBM; range over 3000 km; 1.5-tonne payload.
Agni ranges: Agni-1 700 km, Agni-2 2,000 km, Agni-3 3,000 km, Agni-4 4,000 km, Agni-5 5,000 km.
Also: first Cadet Training Ship 'Krishna' (Yard 18003) launched 16 Feb 2026 at L&T, Kattupalli (Chennai).
Krishna is the first of three Cadet Training Ships.
u0509.hook: Agni ranges: 1 → 700 km, then 2, 3, 4, 5 → thousand km each.
u0509.trap: Agni-III range is about 3,000 km; the longest is Agni-5 at 5,000 km.

mcq.q: Agni-III, successfully test-fired on February 6, 2026, was launched from:
mcq.why: India test-fired Agni-III from the Integrated Test Range, Chandipur, Odisha.

mcq.q: As per the Agni series ranges given in the 2026 report, which Agni missile can strike targets up to 4,000 km?
mcq.why: Agni-4 is capable of striking targets up to 4,000 km; Agni-5 reaches 5,000 km.

u0510.gist: India reportedly inducted INS Aridaman, its third nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine, while stealth frigate INS Taragiri was commissioned at Visakhapatnam.
facts: INS Aridhaman/Aridaman: India's third nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (reported induction).
A larger vessel of about 7,000 tonnes.
Carries more K-15 missiles and K-4 SLBMs that can hit targets 3,500 km away.
Has nearly double the number of VLS tubes of its predecessors.
Stealth frigate INS Taragiri was officially commissioned at Visakhapatnam.
u0510.trap: K-4 (range 3,500 km) and K-15 are submarine-launched missiles; Aridaman is the third such submarine.

mcq.q: INS Aridaman, India's third nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine, can carry K-4 missiles that hit targets about how far away?
mcq.why: The K-4 SLBMs carried by INS Aridaman can hit targets 3,500 km away.

u0511.gist: Dr. Jitendra Singh launched the production version of India's indigenous HANSA-3 NG pilot trainer aircraft at CSIR-NAL, Bengaluru, on November 29, 2025.
facts: Launched November 29, 2025 by Dr. Jitendra Singh, MoS (Independent Charge), Science and Technology.
Developed by CSIR–National Aerospace Laboratories (NAL), Bengaluru.
All-composite airframe (not purely metal).
Meets demand for PPL (Private Pilot Licence) and CPL (Commercial Pilot Licence) training.
First designed by CSIR-NAL in the early 1990s; the new version is much upgraded.

mcq.q: The production version of the indigenous HANSA-3 NG pilot trainer aircraft was launched in November 2025 at:
mcq.why: Dr. Jitendra Singh launched it at CSIR–National Aerospace Laboratories (NAL), Bengaluru.

u0512.gist: DRDO is developing 'Dhvani', a Hypersonic Glide Vehicle that can make sharp manoeuvres at high altitude at speeds above Mach 5.
facts: Developed by DRDO under its advanced hypersonic weapons programme.
Type: Hypersonic Glide Vehicle (HGV).
Speed above Mach 5 (more than 7,400 km/h): current missile defences can hardly intercept it.
Can make sharp, high-speed changes of direction at high altitudes.
Possible range 6,000 to 10,000 kilometers: nearly double the reach of Agni-V ICBM.
u0512.trap: Dhvani is a glide vehicle (HGV), not a ballistic missile like Agni-V.

mcq.q: DRDO's 'Dhvani' hypersonic missile is being developed as which type of system?
mcq.why: Dhvani is designed as a Hypersonic Glide Vehicle (HGV) flying above Mach 5.

u0513.gist: The 7th Global Fintech Fest was held in Mumbai from 8 to 11 September 2026, showing India's fintech growth built on Aadhaar, UPI and DPI.
facts: 7th edition of the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) held in Mumbai, 8 to 11 September 2026.
GFF began in 2020; called the world's largest fintech festival.
Theme: 'Potential to Impact: Agentic AI | Tokenisation | Quantum: Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance'.
Agentic AI: systems that sense, decide and act; Tokenisation: assets as programmable digital units.
India's fintech rise built on Aadhaar, UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI).
u0513.hook: GFF 2026 theme = A-T-Q: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum.

mcq.q: The 7th edition of the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) was held in which city in September 2026?
mcq.why: The 7th edition of GFF was held in Mumbai from 8 to 11 September 2026.

mcq.q: Which three technologies formed the theme of the Global Fintech Fest 2026?
mcq.why: The theme was 'Potential to Impact: Agentic AI | Tokenisation | Quantum'.

u0514.gist: The Indian Army began procuring 'Saksham', an indigenous Counter-Unmanned Aerial System grid made by BEL, to tackle hostile drones.
facts: SAKSHAM = Situational Awareness for Kinetic Soft and Hard Kill Assets Management.
Indigenous C-UAS (counter-drone) grid system developed by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL).
Aim: detect, track, identify and neutralise enemy drones in real time in border areas.
Procurement started by the Indian Army to counter emerging aerial threats.
u0514.hook: SAKSHAM spelt out: Situational Awareness for Kinetic Soft and Hard kill Assets Management.

mcq.q: The 'Saksham' Counter-Unmanned Aerial System grid being procured by the Indian Army was developed by:
mcq.why: Saksham is an indigenous C-UAS grid system developed by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL).

u0515.gist: On October 12, 2026, TRAI released its telecom performance report for the April–June 2026 quarter; internet subscriptions reached 1,114.17 million.
facts: Released by TRAI on October 12, 2026; covers 1st April 2026 to 30th June 2026.
Internet subscriptions: 1,092.79 million (March) to 1,114.17 million (June 2026), up 1.96%.
Total telephone subscriptions 1,348.08 million; tele-density 94.31 per 100 people.
Private operators hold 92.50% of telephone subscriptions; public sector 7.50%.
Monthly wireless ARPU up 1.19% to ₹187.12; rural share fell to 41.24%.
Mobile data use up 8.30% to 84,424 PB; 28.39 GB per subscriber per month.
u0515.trap: Tele-density 94.31 includes machine-to-machine (M2M) links; without M2M it is 84.88.
u0515.check: The source itself notes that rounded totals imply about 1.83% growth in mobile data subscriptions, while the official summary says 1.86%.

mcq.q: As per TRAI's performance indicator report for the quarter ending June 2026, India's overall tele-density was:
mcq.why: Overall tele-density rose from 93.26 to 94.31 connections per 100 people.

mcq.q: As per TRAI's report for April–June 2026, what share of all telephone subscriptions was held by private operators?
mcq.why: Private operators held 92.50%; public sector operators held 7.50%.

u0516.gist: On September 24, 2026, IIT Delhi announced an indigenous micro-GPU for embedded devices, shown on an FPGA, with a chip (ASIC) version planned.
facts: Announced September 24, 2026 by IIT Delhi.
Led by M.Tech students Nammi Akash and M. Ravi Teja under Prof. Jayadeva and Prof. Kaushik Saha.
Custom floating-point GPU engine, built fully in Register Transfer Language (RTL).
Shown on a Spartan-7 FPGA (chip programmable after manufacture); ASIC (task-specific chip) planned.
Targets embedded devices: computers made for specific jobs.
u0516.trap: Demonstrated on an FPGA; the ASIC version is only planned.

mcq.q: The indigenous micro-GPU announced by IIT Delhi in September 2026 was demonstrated on which chip?
mcq.why: The design was mapped to a Spartan-7 FPGA; ASIC development remains planned.

u0517.gist: On 21 September 2026, MoS Anupriya Patel launched the 7th National Formulary of India and announced approval of the Biovigilance Programme of India.
facts: Launched 21 September 2026 by MoS Health Anupriya Patel at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi.
Occasion: 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week, organised by the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC).
Launched: 7th Edition of National Formulary of India (NFI), medical-device safety guidance, ADR-PvPI 2.0 iOS app.
Biovigilance Programme of India: monitors adverse events from products used in organ and tissue transplants.
Covers products given to both donors and recipients.
u0517.trap: 7th = edition of NFI; 6th = National Pharmacovigilance Week.

mcq.q: The Biovigilance Programme of India, approved in 2026, extends safety monitoring to products used in:
mcq.why: It covers medicines and biological products used in organ and tissue transplantation.

mcq.q: Which edition of the National Formulary of India (NFI) was launched in September 2026?
mcq.why: Anupriya Patel launched the 7th Edition of the NFI on 21 September 2026.

u0518.gist: The Union Cabinet approved the BHAVYA-Rasayan Scheme with Rs.3,030 crore to set up three dedicated Chemical Parks from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.
facts: BHAVYA = Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana; Rasayan scheme for three Chemical Parks.
Announced in Union Budget FY 2026–27; approved by the Union Cabinet chaired by PM Modi.
Total outlay Rs.3,030 crore: Rs.3,000 crore for infrastructure, Rs. 30 crore administrative.
Runs for 5 years: FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.
Centre gives up to Rs.1,000 crore per park; State must give at least Rs.500 crore.
u0518.hook: Three 3s: three parks, Rs.3,030 crore total, Rs.3,000 crore for infrastructure.
u0518.trap: Rs.1,000 crore = Centre's maximum grant per park; Rs.500 crore = State's minimum share.

mcq.q: What is the total financial outlay of the BHAVYA-Rasayan Scheme for Chemical Parks?
mcq.why: Total outlay is Rs.3,030 crore: Rs.3,000 crore infrastructure plus Rs. 30 crore administrative.

mcq.q: How many dedicated Chemical Parks will be set up under the BHAVYA-Rasayan Scheme?
mcq.why: The scheme is for establishing three dedicated Chemical Parks.

u0519.gist: Ladakh commissioned India's first geothermal wells, two 1000-metre-deep wells at Puga Valley, paving the way for India's first geothermal power plant.
facts: Two 1000-metre-deep geothermal wells at Puga Valley, Ladakh: India's first, in the cold desert.
Altitude: 14,000 feet.
Inaugurated by VK Saxena, Lt Governor of Ladakh.
Will support a 1 MW pilot geothermal power project at Puga: India's first demonstration-scale project.
Maximum temperature of 135 degrees Celsius recorded at 400 metres depth.
u0519.hook: Puga: 2 wells, 1000 m deep, for 1 MW.
u0519.trap: 135°C was recorded at 400 m depth, although the wells are 1000 m deep.

mcq.q: India's first geothermal wells, commissioned by the Ladakh administration for a pilot power project, are located in which valley?
mcq.why: Two 1000-metre-deep wells were commissioned at Puga Valley, Ladakh.

u0520.gist: Bharat Electricity Summit 2026 was held at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, on 19-22 March 2026; it released resource adequacy and transmission plans.
facts: Held 19 to 22 March 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi.
Theme: 'Electrifying Growth. Empowering Sustainability. Connecting Globally.'
Released: National Resource Adequacy Plan; Transmission Plan for over 900 GW non-fossil capacity by 2035–36.
FY 2025–26: record non-fossil addition of 55.29 GW (solar 44.61 GW, wind 6.05 GW).
As of 31 March 2026: total capacity 5,32,740 MW; non-fossil share 53.2%.
FY 2025–26 energy deficit only 0.03%; peak deficit only 0.01%.
u0520.hook: 'One Nation – One Grid – One Frequency': the world's largest synchronous national grid.
u0520.trap: 52,537 MW is capacity added only up to 31 January 2026; the full-year non-fossil addition is 55.29 GW.

mcq.q: As of 31 March 2026, what share of India's total installed power generation capacity was non-fossil?
mcq.why: Non-fossil capacity was 2,83,468 MW, forming 53.2% of total installed capacity.

mcq.q: Bharat Electricity Summit 2026 (19-22 March) was held at which venue?
mcq.why: The Summit was held from 19 to 22 March 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi.

u0521.gist: Approval was granted (Finance Ministry release, October 4, 2025) for Maitri II, India's proposed fourth Antarctic research station in East Antarctica, ready by 2032.
facts: Approval announced in a Ministry of Finance press release on October 4, 2025.
Maitri II: India's proposed fourth research station, in East Antarctica; to be ready by 2032.
First station: Dakshin Gangotri; active stations: Maitri (since 1989) and Bharati (since 2012).
Maitri is on the Schirmacher Oasis, a 20 km ice-free stretch, about 100 km inland.
Project executed by the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa.
u0521.hook: Antarctic line-up: Dakshin Gangotri → Maitri (1989) → Bharati (2012) → Maitri II (2032).
u0521.trap: Maitri II will be the fourth station, though only two (Maitri, Bharati) are active now.

mcq.q: Maitri II, approved in October 2025, will be India's which research station in Antarctica?
mcq.why: Maitri II will be India's proposed fourth research station, in East Antarctica.

mcq.q: Which body is executing the Maitri II Antarctic research station project?
mcq.why: The project is being executed by the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa.

u0522.gist: Short items: India's first shipbuilding SPV in Tamil Nadu, WAVES Animation Bazaar with India Joy 2025 in Hyderabad, and IISF 2025 in Panchkula.
facts: NSHIP, TN (National Shipbuilding & Heavy Industries Park): India's first SPV for a mega shipbuilding cluster.
WAVES Animation Bazaar and 8th India Joy 2025: two-day event inaugurated November 1, 2025, Hyderabad.
Supported by Telangana government, Telangana VFX, Animation and Gaming Association and Union I&B Ministry.
11th India International Science Festival (IISF): December 6-9, 2025, Panchkula, Haryana.
IISF 2025 theme: 'Vigyan Se Samruddhi: for Atmanirbhar Bharat'.

mcq.q: The 11th India International Science Festival (IISF) 2025 was held in:
mcq.why: The 11th edition of IISF was held from December 6-9, 2025 in Panchkula, Haryana.

mcq.q: India's first Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for developing a mega shipbuilding cluster, NSHIP, is in which state?
mcq.why: The National Shipbuilding & Heavy Industries Park, Tamil Nadu (NSHIP, TN) is the first such SPV.
